subject: Privatescape: private/dedicated deployment - isolation diagrams & evidence
messages:
From: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@privatescape.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-09-29T16:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: network isolation evidence for Dedicated/Private

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the walkthrough last week. As we prepare for our SOC 2 scoping, the auditors have asked for a concise security architecture package showing network isolation between our tenants and Redwood's control plane for the Private deployment we're evaluating. Specifically they want: two-page network diagram(s) (logical + simplified dataflow), an isolation narrative that explains how control-plane traffic is segmented, and any existing proofs for airlock/egress controls.

Can you send a single packet we can hand to the auditors (PDF or Drive folder) and a short Q&A answering whether workloads on Dedicated can be pinned to tenant-only subnets and what fallback routing looks like?

We have a deadline of Oct 15 for the auditor kick-off. Appreciate any prioritized artifacts.

Thanks,
Alex Taylor
Head of Infrastructure | PrivateScape
security@privatescape.com

--
Alex T.
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Taylor <alex.taylor@privatescape.com>
Date: 2026-09-30T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: network isolation evidence for Dedicated/Private

Alex —

Thanks for the clear ask and the timeline. We can assemble an auditor-friendly packet. Plan below:

- Deliverables: 1) 2-sheet logical diagram (control plane vs data plane), 2) one-page isolation narrative, 3) short Q&A for SOC 2 scope (tenant pinning, egress controls, KMS boundaries), 4) example airlock/topology PDF.
- Format: consolidated PDF + Drive folder with source PNGs and the SOC2 Q&A (spreadsheet).
- Timing: draft packet to you by 2026-10-03, final by 2026-10-09 to give you time before Oct 15.

Quick answers to the two bullets you mentioned:
- Can Dedicated be pinned to tenant-only subnets? Yes — Dedicated pools are provisioned into isolated VPCs with explicit routing tables; we create tenant-scoped subnets and security group policies.
- Fallback routing: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant in another capacity tier is policy-driven and only used when configured; cross-tenant routing is blocked by default.

I'll assemble the packet but loop in Engineering for the diagrams and PCI for the wording on the airlock.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Security Architecture
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-30T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Privatescape evidence - diagram + QnA (internal coordination)

Team — forwarding Privatescape's auditor ask. Can you help with two items in the attached packet?

1) Stephanie — can you produce a simplified two-pane diagram (left: control plane, right: data plane) with arrows for KV cache, model pull, and egress points. Keep it high level for auditors; include labels for VPCs, NAT gateways, and KMS boundary.

2) Ben — can you prepare a one-page narrative explaining tenant pinning and the fallback policy (policy names, expected latencies, and routing constraints)? Also pull any precedent evidence we can share (redacted topology screenshots).

Attachments to include: network-map-v2.png (diagram), airlock-topology.pdf (airlock proof), privatescape-soc2-qna.xlsx (questionnaire template). Tag the Drive link when ready.

On urgency — Kimberly's draft to Privatescape is due EOD 2026-10-03.

Thanks,
Kim
